name: Chrysler/SRT 6.2 L supercharged Hemi 'Hellcat' V8 (2015 Dodge Challenger and Charger SRT Hellcat)
induction: supercharged (IHI twin-screw, 3-lobe and 5-lobe rotors, two liquid-to-air charge coolers)
summary: A Gen III Hemi cross-plane V8 (big two-valve hemispherical chambers, pushrods) with an IHI twin-screw blower on top and the throttle at the blower's inlet. Cross-plane V8 burble with a screw-blower whine at about 11.8 crank orders.

layout.note: Not stated on a page read; the Gen III Hemi's 90-degree bank angle is from memory. 'engsim pins' with the sourced firing order gives shared pins and even 90-degree intervals only at 90 degrees for a cross-plane crank.

bore_mm.note: SAE Mobility Engineering: 103.9 x 90.9 mm. EngineLabs (chief engineer interview): 4.09 in bore, 3.58 in stroke, 6,166 cc; Wards' Challenger spec box: 103.9 x 90.9 mm. 4.09 in = 103.886 mm is used.

stroke_mm.note: EngineLabs: 3.58 in (90.93 mm, used; it gives 6,166 cc with the 4.09 in bore). Wards' engine article says 3.57 in; Muscle Car Club 3.578 in.

compression_ratio.note: EngineLabs: 9.5:1. Wards' Challenger spec box and Muscle Car Club agree.

rod_length_mm.note: Not found. Estimate 158.6 mm (6.243 in), the Gen III Hemi rod length from memory, not checked against a source.

firing_order.note: SlashGear (Joe Capraro, 22 Aug 2024), secondary: 'The firing order ... goes in the sequence 1-8-4-3-6-5-7-2', 'the same for all third-generation HEMI engines', and the list includes 'the supercharged 6.2-liter — which goes by Demon, Hellcat, and Redeye'. Numbering from the same page: odd cylinders 1, 3, 5, 7 on the driver's side front to back, even 2, 4, 6, 8 on the passenger side. No Chrysler document found (sdparts.com PDF 404; dodgegarage.com redirected to dodge.com, which refuses bots, not followed; rerev.com 403).

crank.value: cross-plane, four throws at 90 degrees, each pin shared by one cylinder from each bank
crank.note: Not stated on a page read; every Gen III Hemi is a cross-plane V8 with an even 90-degree firing (from memory). 'engsim pins' confirms that this firing order on that crank gives shared pins 1-2, 3-4, 5-6, 7-8 and even 90-degree intervals.

valves_per_cylinder.note: Two valves: Wards: hollow intake valves, sodium-filled exhaust valves.

intake_valve_dia_mm.note: Muscle Car Club (Austin Parsons, 9 Dec 2023), secondary: intake 2.14 in (54.36 mm, my conversion).

exhaust_valve_dia_mm.note: Muscle Car Club: exhaust 1.65 in (41.91 mm), sodium-filled.

intake_lift_mm.note: EngineLabs (chief engineer interview): 14.25 mm intake, 14.0 mm exhaust. Muscle Car Club gives 0.571 / 0.536 in (14.5 / 13.6 mm); the interview is used.

intake_duration_deg.note: Muscle Car Club, secondary: intake duration 278, exhaust 304, overlap 51, centreline 109. The lift these are measured at is not stated (advertised durations); they are entered as seat to seat. Events derived by me: intake opens 30 BTDC, closes 68 ABDC (centre 109 ATDC); exhaust closes 21 ATDC (overlap 51 = 30 + 21), opens 103 BBDC; lobe separation 120.

variable_valve_timing.note: EngineLabs mentions cam phasing; Wards: variable valve timing. Not modelled: the fixed cam above is used.

redline_rpm.note: supercars.net (2015 Charger SRT Hellcat): redline 6,200; motortopia: 6,200 rpm. Used as the limiter.

peak_power_kw.note: SAE Mobility Engineering: 'SAE J1349-rated at 707 hp (527 kW) and 650 lb·ft (881 N·m)'. PR Newswire (Chrysler release): 707 hp and 650 lb-ft.

peak_power_rpm.note: Wards' Challenger spec box: 707 hp @ 6,000 rpm; supercars.net and motortopia (Charger): 6,000. Muscle Car Club: 'between 6,000 and 6,400 rpm'.

peak_torque_rpm.note: Conflict: supercars.net and motortopia (Charger) give 4,800 rpm; Wards' Challenger spec box gives 4,000 rpm. 4,800 is used (two pages, and the Charger is the vehicle modelled); the fit at 4,000 is reported too.

intake_type.value: supercharger on top with integrated charge coolers; single throttle
intake_type.note: EngineLabs: one intercooler on each side; Muscle Car Club: two air-to-water intercoolers built into the blower housing; SAE: integral charge coolers.

throttle_position.value: before the supercharger (not stated on a page read)
throttle_position.note: None of the pages read says where the throttle sits. Before the blower, at its inlet, is the usual Hemi Hellcat layout from memory, unverified. Modelled that way.

supercharger.value: IHI twin-screw (Lysholm), 3-lobe male and 5-lobe female rotors
supercharger.note: EngineLabs: IHI twin-screw, 3-lobe male and 5-lobe female rotors. SAE: IHI Lysholm twin-screw.

blower_displacement_l.unit: L per revolution (of the rotor the drive ratio refers to; my reading)
blower_displacement_l.note: SAE: 'Displacing 2380 cm³'. Conflict: Wards: 2.04 L per revolution; 2,380 is used (SAE, and the boost check below). The simulator counts displacement per male-rotor revolution; my conversion: 2.38 L per revolution of the 2.36:1 rotor, which is the 5-lobe rotor (below), is 2.38 x 3/5 = 1.428 L per male revolution. Either way the swept volume per crank revolution is 2.38 x 2.36 = 5.62 L.

drive_ratio.note: SAE: drive ratio '2.36:1', '14,600-rpm maximum operating speed'; EngineLabs: 'Drive 2.36:1 over crank', low rotor maximum 14,500 rpm, high rotor up to 24,000 rpm. My reasoning: 2.36 x 6,200 rpm (redline) = 14,630, the low rotor's maximum, so 2.36 belongs to the slower rotor; in a 3+5 screw the 3-lobe male turns 5/3 as fast as the 5-lobe female, 3.93 x crank, 24,400 rpm at 6,200, which matches EngineLabs' 24,000. The simulator's ratio is the male rotor's: 3.933. Conflict: Wards gives the blower 14,600 rpm at 6,000 engine rpm and the secondary rotor 'just under 20,000', which fits neither reading.

boost_psi.note: SAE: 'up to 11.6 psi (80 kPa)', controlled by the bypass valve; Wards: 11.6 psi (80 kPa); EngineLabs: 'nearly 12 pounds', 'up to 11.6 psi'. No rpm given. Used as the check.

bypass_valve.note: EngineLabs: electric bypass using a throttle body; Wards: bypass when cruising. Its control law is not published; modelled as the simulator's vacuum bypass with derived settings (estimate), which does not limit boost.

overrun_clutch.value: one-way clutch (decoupler) on the blower pulley
overrun_clutch.note: EngineLabs: one-way decoupler; Wards: one-way clutch. Not modelled: the simulator's blower is locked to the crank.

exhaust_notes.note: EngineLabs: double-wall manifolds; SAE: active exhaust. Sizes not found.

sources.what: SAE Mobility Engineering, Lindsay Brooke, 21 May 2014: SAE rating, bore and stroke, IHI blower displacement, drive ratio and speed, boost, throttle, charge coolers, final drives.

EngineLabs, Mike Magda, 24 July 2014: interview with the Hellcat engine's chief engineer (bore, stroke, compression, rotors, drive ratio, rotor speeds, boost, throttle, bypass, decoupler, cam lift and phasing).
WardsAuto, 6 Oct 2014, Hemi Hellcat engine: stroke, blower displacement and rotor speeds (conflicting), boost, bypass, one-way clutch, valves.
WardsAuto Challenger SRT Hellcat review with a specification box: power and torque speeds, bore and stroke, compression, gearboxes, curb weight.
Muscle Car Club, Austin Parsons, 9 Dec 2023 (enthusiast, secondary): valve sizes, cam durations and centreline, peak power speed range.
SlashGear, Joe Capraro, 22 Aug 2024 (secondary): Gen III Hemi firing order and numbering, including the supercharged 6.2.
Chrysler's release on PR Newswire: 707 hp and 650 lb-ft.
supercars.net, 2015 Dodge Charger SRT Hellcat: power and torque speeds, redline, eight-speed ratios, final drive.
motortopia, 2015 Dodge Charger SRT Hellcat: power and torque speeds, curb weight, final drive.

vehicle.name: Dodge Charger SRT Hellcat (2015)

curb_kg.note: motortopia: 4,575 lb (2,075 kg, my conversion). The Challenger, which had the manual, weighs 4,439 lb in Wards' spec box.

gear_count.note: Eight-speed automatic only on the 2015 Charger SRT Hellcat.

final_drive.note: supercars.net and motortopia: 2.62. SAE: 2.62 with the automatic, 3.70 with the manual.

tyre.note: Not found on a page read; the wheel radius is left to the default.

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Dodge Challenger (2008)': front engine, rear-wheel drive; the Charger shares the platform (my inference; Charger article pending).

top_speed_kmh.note: Not used: the final drive is sourced.

vehicle.alternative_manual: 2015 Challenger SRT Hellcat with the Tremec TR-6060 six-speed manual and a 3.70 final drive (SAE); its gear ratios were not found on any page read, so the Charger with the automatic is modelled.
